title: A square-root law for equitable coloring
summary: An equitable $k$-coloring of a graph partitions its vertex set into $k$ independent sets whose sizes differ by at most one; the least such $k$ is the equitable chromatic number $\chie(G)$. Every known bound on $\chie$ valid for all graphs, beginning with the Hajnal--Szemerédi theorem, is linear in the maximum degree $Δ$, and the star $K_{1,Δ}$, for which $\chie=\ceil{Δ/2}+1$, shows that no general bound below $Δ/2$ exists.
